actions.note: Added 2026-10-01 (root-caused via bot-log-doctor + Preston's own observation — see project_bot_train_troops_fp_capacity_cap memory): tapping Start Training either starts training (the button disappears and the Speed Up button takes its place next) or is rejected because this camp's unit capacity is maxed (the button just stays on screen). These two outcomes are mutually exclusive, so checking whether Start Training persists after the tap is enough to detect the capacity-cap case directly, instead of silently burning ~15s running the Speed Up tap + 6x retry loop against a camp that never started training.

Explicit tap on the real green 'Speed Up' button to open the item-selection popup. Previously this step blindly retried btn_start_train_troops.png (the 'Train' button) a second time, which is visually near-identical to this Speed Up button (same green/rounded/white-text style) -- it was opening the popup only by accidental mismatch, not reliably.

Keep tapping the speed-up button until it's no longer present — each tap consumes a speed-up until training is instantly complete. Retries widened to 6x1.0s (~7s) so a slow-rendering popup isn't misread as 'button already gone'. Deliberately does NOT run dismiss_ads.json first — btn_ad_close.png is a generic X that matches this same Speed Up dialog's own close button and was closing the popup before this check ever ran

actions.note: Same capacity-cap detection as the Assaulter/Rider blocks above. Shooter is the last troop type in this task, so on a maxed capacity this jumps to step 70 (one past the final action, index 69) to finish the task cleanly via a normal skip_to rather than falling through to ABORT_TASK. That distinction matters here: army_expansion.json's run_task call for this task has no contain_abort, so an ABORT_TASK would propagate up and skip fp_reward_collection.json and the second training pass (start_train_troops_fp.json) entirely — a routine 'this one camp is maxed' state should never do that.
